AUTHOR: Liu, MX; Wu, YJ; Li, RX; Lin, C
TITLE: LFN-YOLO: precision underwater small object detection via a lightweight reparameterized approach
REGION: Limfjorden, Denmark (Brackish); also URPC (China) and TrashCan (JAMSTEC) without fish-specific focus
SPECIES: Brackish classes: crab, normal-sized fish, small fish, starfish, shrimp, jellyfish
DATA: Brackish dataset (11,205 images); URPC 2021 (7,543 images, no fish); TrashCan (7,212 images); fish-fry tank deployment demo
V_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'the presence of numerous suspended particles in the water results in image blurring, reduced contrast, and even scattering artifacts' (Brackish dataset)
D_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and testing sets in an 8:1:1 ratio.'
R_EV: Sec. 5.3: 'we trained both the LFN-YOLO and YOLOv8n models using the Brackish dataset... recognition scenario being a 200L fish tank' (qualitative results only, Figs 10-11)
E_EV: Abstract: 'the mAP@0.5 reached 74.1%, 97.5%, and 66.2%, respectively' (detection metrics only)
ARCH: LFN-YOLO: YOLOv8n with RepGhost backbone, SPD-Conv, GFPN neck, CLLAHead with DFL
METR: Precision, recall, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, FPS, parameters, GFLOPs
NOTE: Included on the basis of Brackish (allowed monitoring dataset with fish classes); URPC (no fish) and TrashCan are benchmark/other sets. Brackish was randomly re-split 8:1:1 by the authors (not the predefined split). Edge deployment: Brackish-trained model run in a 200 L fish-fry tank, qualitative only -> R1=Y, R3=N per qualitative-external rule; TrashCan is trained/tested separately (not external).
